verdict_summary.notes: All 14 SARIF results carry the single ruleId py/augur/zope/pass1-path-traversal (one CodeQL run, driver 'CodeQL'); no diagnostics, no CodeQL built-in security queries and no other CWE results are mixed into this batch (instruction item 10: confirmed). 11 of 14 alerts share one systematic FP root cause (see fp_root_cause).

fp_root_cause.title: MySources.isRequestSubscriptValue over-matches os.environ subscripts
fp_root_cause.mechanism: MySources.qll isRequestLikeObject (lines 333-337) accepts any receiver that is a Name in [request, REQUEST, environ] OR an Attribute whose getName() is in [request, REQUEST, environ, form]. 'os.environ' is an Attribute named 'environ', so os.environ['INSTANCE_HOME'] (src/App/FindHomes.py:18) and os.environ['CLIENT_HOME'] (src/App/FindHomes.py:30) match isRequestSubscriptValue as if they were WSGI request-environ lookups. These are process/deployment environment variables (operator boundary), exactly the env_config family that labels.json classifies as role 'none' / fp (e.g. p1-src-001: 'Environment-variable read (operator/deployment configuration)') and that query_generation_notes.md section 2 claims is deliberately NOT modeled ('Config/CLI sink sites have no reachable source and cannot alert', section 7). The claim is falsified by the formal run: the accidental source reaches the config-derived sinks through App/config.py:60-61 (clienthome/instancehome properties) into Extensions.py, ObjectManager.py, startup.py, userfolder.py, zcml.py. Affected alerts: #0, #1, #3, #4, #5, #6, #10, #11, #12, #13 (all their codeFlows start at FindHomes.py:18/:30). Finding #2 additionally contains one request-derived path (manage_exportObject id) reviewed on its own merits below.
fp_root_cause.fix_direction: Constrain the subscript/get receiver to the request object itself (e.g. require the receiver Name 'environ' to be a parameter/local bound from the WSGI boundary, or exclude an Attribute whose object is the Name 'os'). Not applied here - this review modifies no query artifacts.

publisher_dot_segment_normalization.evidence: PATH_INFO is split on '/' and each segment is filtered: literal '.' and empty segments are dropped (line 378-379), a literal '..' segment pops the previous clean segment (line 380-381) and never reaches traverseName. The only HTTP publish entry (src/ZPublisher/WSGIPublisher.py:252-255: path = request.get('PATH_INFO'); request.traverse(path, validated_hook=validate_user)) goes through this loop, so no URL segment delivered to publishTraverse/get can be '..' or contain '/'.
publisher_dot_segment_normalization.assessment: This is a real pre-access mitigation that neutralizes the classic ../ token on every in-repo HTTP traversal route, but it is NOT a root-containment check (no canonicalization/containment on the joined result) and it does not filter backslash segments ('..\x' survives the clean loop) or drive-relative segments.

restricted_traverse_alternate_route.evidence: restrictedTraverse/unrestrictedTraverse split on '/' and handle '..' as upward acquisition traversal themselves; segments on this route likewise cannot contain '/' or be a literal '..'.
restricted_traverse_alternate_route.assessment: The alternate (request-data driven, e.g. OFS/Cache.py:522) traversal route carries the same segment constraints.

percent_decoding.evidence: Percent-decoding happens in the WSGI server before PATH_INFO is set (PEP 3333); WSGIPublisher.py:312-338 only re-encodes latin-1->utf-8. A single-decoded '%2e%2e' becomes a literal '..' segment and is removed by the clean loop; a double-encoded '%252e%252e' stays the literal string '%2e%2e' (no second unquote on the resource.py get path - unquote is only used for URL rendering in Resource.__call__, resource.py:50). No double-decode bypass found.
percent_decoding.assessment: Decoding factors do not change the access target beyond what the clean loop already handles.

checkvalidid.evidence: checkValidId rejects empty/non-str, control/angle chars (bad_id regex line 81), literal '.' and '..' (line 98), leading '_' (line 101), 'aq_' prefix (line 105), trailing '__' (line 108), '@@'/'++' prefixes (line 112), 'REQUEST' (line 131) and ANY id containing '/' (lines 133-135).
checkvalidid.assessment: The label rationale for p1-snk-343 and query_generation_notes.md section 5 claim checkValidId 'does not reject / or embedded ..' - this is factually wrong for this source revision: '/' IS rejected (line 133). Backslash is NOT rejected, leaving a Windows-only separator-variation residual for ids.

Object ids are validated at creation time by checkValidId (ObjectManager.py:84-135): '/' is rejected at :133-135 and a literal '..' at :98 - this corrects the p1-snk-343 label rationale, which wrongly claims checkValidId does not reject '/'. Residual (unblocked, documented): backslash ids are not rejected by checkValidId's bad_id regex (:81), so on a Windows ntpath deployment an object id like '..\\..\\x' makes join(:621) escape clienthome
preconditions: Caller holds import_export_objects permission (Manager by default)

findings.reasoning: The request->write taint flow is real (item 1/2 pass), and the sink is a genuine write (item 3 passes). But every precondition is Manager-gated: creating a traversable object id and invoking the export both require Manager, the exported content is a ZODB serialization (not arbitrary attacker bytes), and on POSIX the write is confined to clienthome. This is the authorized operation of the export feature (review item 8), not an unauthorized file write. The only escape vector (Windows backslash ids) requires Manager twice. Judged likely_fp as a vulnerability; recorded residual risk keeps confidence at 0.75 rather than 0.95. Note the label p1-snk-343 rationale contains a factual error about checkValidId ('/' IS rejected at ObjectManager.py:133) that inflated this alert's candidate rating.

real_vulnerability_hit_check.question: Is the known real vulnerability (commit 1f8456bf1f908ea46012537d52bd7e752a532c91, GHSA-5pr9-v234-jw36, CWE-22) hit by any formal Pass 1 alert?
real_vulnerability_hit_check.vulnerability_mechanism_from_provided_di: TAL path-expression traversal does not reject path items starting with '_'. The fix adds: name == '_' -> DeprecationWarning; name.startswith('_') -> raise NotFound. Before the fix, a ZPT/TAL path expression (or python-expression path traversal) could traverse to underscore-prefixed names, reaching protected internals/attributes (untrusted-module access), with the precondition that untrusted users can add/edit Zope Page Templates through the web (default: Manager only).
analysis: None of the 14 formal Pass 1 alerts is located in src/Products/PageTemplates/Expressions.py or touches boboAwareZopeTraverse/traverse/traversePathElement - the fixed functions produce no Pass 1 alert at all.

Mechanism mismatch with the Pass 1 sink model: the vulnerability's sink is object/module-namespace access (attribute lookup on '_'-prefixed names via traversePathElement / restrictedTraverse, yielding untrusted module objects), not a filesystem path argument. The MySinks set (open / os.path* / shutil / filestream_iterator / importFile / resource factory) contains no sink this flow can reach - indeed no filesystem path is materialized at any point of the vulnerable flow.

Source-side mismatch: the tainted path items originate from TAL expression text inside Page Templates (authored by whoever can add/edit ZPTs - Manager by default, untrusted only on specific site configurations). The Pass 1 source model has no 'TAL path item' source; ZopePageTemplate ZMI form parameters (id/file, ZopePageTemplate.py:370) are modeled, but the template text->expression compilation path into Expressions.py traversal is outside both the source and sink models and outside stdlib taint steps (mapply/expression compilation are documented unmodeled dispatch gaps in query_generation_notes.md section 6).
Database coverage is not the blocker: src/Products/PageTemplates/Expressions.py is inside the Zope_vuln source tree, so the miss is a source/sink-scope miss, not a coverage miss.

Classification note: the advisory is labeled CWE-22, but the abused 'path' is the ZODB/module namespace, not the filesystem; a filesystem-sink pass (this Pass 1 model) is structurally incapable of detecting it. The related in-repo traversal guards (Traversable.py:213-215 already rejects leading-underscore names in restrictedTraverse - the same hardening the 5.2 fix applied to the TAL expression path) show the defense existed on one route but not on the PageTemplates expression route.
real_vulnerability_hit_check.verdict: MISSED - the real vulnerability is not hit by any of the 14 formal Pass 1 alerts. This comparison used only the commit data provided in the task prompt; no PyVul ground-truth files, fix diffs or CVE descriptions were read, and this comparison was not used to promote or demote any alert verdict above.
